headline.label: The swap test: same-price trades the model would have made
headline.unit: more points above replacement per swap over three seasons
headline.detail: 65 swaps made each February 2021-2023: three seasons later the player bought delivered that much more above a replacement-level player at his position, ahead in 68% of swaps; in wins +0.46 per swap, 71% won (the model had said +0.78); 123 raw points, a number that mixes positions

headline.label: The mispricing column, net of regression to the mean
headline.unit: ranks better than their market rank predicts
headline.detail: players the model called cheap finished that many ranks better than a player at their market rank usually does, the ones it called rich 6.8 worse; on the disagreed players the model's rank sat 1.6 ranks closer to the finish than the market's; the raw gap (+14.4 / -10.8) is inflated by regression to the mean (a model with no skill scores about +10 on it)

headline.label: Rest of this season: ordering players by the points above replacement they go on to deliver
headline.detail: vs the provider's own projection 0.614 and the market's 0.615 at week 3; 0.554 vs 0.49 / 0.462 at week 13; cohorts 2021-2024; a dynasty price is not a rest-of-season ranking, so the provider's projection is the yardstick that counts

headline.label: Next season, from a mid-season snapshot: ordering by points above replacement
headline.detail: vs the market's 0.558 at week 3; 0.606 vs 0.587 at week 13: behind or level with the market early in the season, ahead from week 9

headline.label: 3 years out: ordering by the wins players then delivered (a statistical tie)
headline.detail: vs the market's 0.675 on 369 priced player-cohorts, priced each February 2021-2023; the difference sits inside its noise (a 95 % interval of about −0.02 to +0.06); the market is better on under-25s and rookies, the model on ages 25-32 and running backs

headline.label: Career projection, 3 years ahead: error vs an age-decay curve
headline.detail: −30% vs repeating last season (a baseline attrition punishes); 7,338 player-seasons since 2010, seasons never played counted as zero; the 2026-10-01 evaluation (the tree walk-forward, not the production model)

method: walk-forward: the model rebuilt with only what was known at the time, scored on what the players then delivered; KTC is the yardstick, never an input (the in-season model does read the providers' projections and preseason ADP since 2026-10-12; the career model the swap test validates reads neither); the unit of evidence is the test year, and the review of 2026-10-13 (docs/MODEL_REVIEW_2026-10-13.md) re-derived every number here
